text.p: Tropical Cyclone Melanie, in the southern Indian Ocean, has become a major threat to shipping. Top winds are near 110 mph. Strengthening is expected during the next 24 hours when top winds may reach 120 mph. The storm is currently centered near 10.5s/85.0e, moving west at 5 mph. A turn to the southwest is expected during this period.

Tropical Cyclone 07B has top winds near 35 mph and is centered near 16.1n/88.7e, and moving west about 7 mph. This system is expected to intensify during th enext 36-48 hours with top winds reaching 55-60 mph by the time the storm makes landfall along the East Central coast of India in about 48 hours, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall.
Heavy rain associated with dissipating Tropical Depression 35W over Thailand may result in local flash flooding during the next 12 hours before conditions improve and rain ends.

A tropical disturbance centered southeast of Guam is nearly stationary but has a good chance of further development. This system may become a threat to shipping and eventually to Guam or the southern Mariana Islands.
Another disturbance east of Mindanao, Philippines, is being watched for further development.
A tropical wave in the western Caribbean may produce heavy rain and local flash flooding over eastern Central America.
